subject: Model improvement exclusion & LATAM residency evidence — pilot onboarding
messages:
From: Mariana Santos <mariana@catalyst.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Andres Rios <andres.rios@saludlatam.cl>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: LATAM pilot - onboarding asks on model improvement exclusion and residency

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency numbers. Before we kick off the pilot in Chile and Argentina, procurement and security asked for concrete evidence of two items we need to close:

1) Model improvement exclusion (we need to ensure our interactions will not be used to update or fine-tune any model).
2) Data residency / transfer path for logs and exports (for a subset of interactions we need onshore routing and a way to export transcripts to our SFTP).

Can you send an "ops evidence" pack showing: the flagging mechanism you use to mark no-improve interactions (how it's enforced end-to-end), a simple dataflow diagram showing where raw requests and ephemeral KV are stored, and the proposed SFTP export path (with an example routing and retention policy)? Procurement also wants a short note about whether any subcontractors will access raw interactions.

Attachments would be great (diagram, checklist). If we can get this by Monday it helps speed contracting.

Thanks — Mariana
CatalystHealth (on behalf of SaludLatam)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mariana Santos <mariana@catalyst.ai>
Cc: Andres Rios <andres.rios@saludlatam.cl>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LATAM pilot - onboarding asks on model improvement exclusion and residency

Hi Mariana — appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, full pack attached.

- Model improvement exclusion: Redwood supports an explicit per-request "model_improvement=false" flag. When set, the runtime routes the interaction through a non-retained KV path and marks it with a policy tag that prevents any telemetry or training pipelines from consuming the content. This is enforced at the routing layer and validated in the auditing pipeline — we include sample audit logs in the pack.

- Dataflow & residency: For your pilot we propose: primary inference in us-west (fastest region for our infra), with an onshore SFTP export lane in Santiago (managed by your SFTP endpoint). Sensitive transcripts marked for residency are copied into a short-lived export bucket in the Santiago tenant, encrypted with your onshore KMS (customer-managed key). We outline the SFTP handshake and retention TTLs in the diagram.

- Subprocessors: the only subprocessors that would see raw interactions for this flow are (1) our log aggregator for operational tracing (it only sees masked fields unless marked otherwise) and (2) the SFTP connector endpoint during export. Both are listed in the pack and we propose an attestation step.

I attached: 1) latam-dataflow-diagram.pdf (high-level flows), 2) ops-evidence-checklist.xlsx (audit samples, log snippet examples), and 3) a short technical note.

If procurement needs a DocuSign addendum with the model improvement exclusion language, say the word and we'll generate the redline. Timeline: we can assemble the exportable evidence and provide the secure files by Monday EOD Pacific if you confirm it's OK to share sample masked logs for the audit.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0126

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Mariana Santos <mariana@catalyst.ai>, Andres Rios <andres.rios@saludlatam.cl>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LATAM pilot - onboarding asks on model improvement exclusion and residency

Hi Mariana / Andres — looping in technical privacy & ops details.

A couple of clarifications and what we'll include in the evidence pack:

- Enforcement model: the "model_improvement=false" flag is sticky for the lifetime of a session and is implemented as a routing attribute at the API gateway. Any requests with that attribute are excluded from data capture queues that feed training or evaluation systems. We will provide a sample policy rule and an endpoint trace showing exclusion.

- Ephemeral KV & prefixes: user session KV is ephemeral by default (TTL = 30 minutes for pilot), and any prefix that could contain PII is redacted unless explicitly allowed. We'll include a KV TTL dump and redaction rules.

- SFTP export & KMS: For onshore copies we will encrypt with the customer-provided KMS key via a cross-account key policy. The export job uses a short-lived service account (auditable) that writes to your SFTP. We'll attach the subprocessor list and the scaffolding for an attestation signed by our Ops team.

- Evidence items we will attach: sample audit log (redacted), routing rule sample, subprocessor inventory, SFTP handshake sample (FTP user, ephemeral creds workflow), and a mapping of data fields we keep vs discard.

David, this is probably a good candidate for a minimal attestation letter from Security and a procurement SOW addendum. Karthik — happy to help author the attestation.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Andres Rios <andres.rios@saludlatam.cl>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Mariana Santos <mariana@catalyst.ai>, Procurement <procure@saludlatam.cl>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LATAM pilot - onboarding asks on model improvement exclusion and residency

Thanks everyone — that answers most questions. Procurement asked for two final items before we route the addendum:

1) A one-paragraph attestation signed by Redwood Security that interactions flagged as "no-improve" are excluded from any model improvement pipelines (this can be a PDF).
2) A sample DocuSign addendum (we'll need the exact clause) so our legal team can review and attach to the SOW.

If you can provide the attestation and a draft addendum by Wednesday, we can finish internal approvals and kick off the pilot integration the following week. Also confirming we received the attachments you sent (latam-dataflow-diagram.pdf, ops-evidence-checklist.xlsx).

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/placeholder

Cheers,
Andres (on behalf of SaludLatam procurement)
